observations: Two black, rectangular power banks lying on a concrete floor.
The top unit has a large piece of yellowish tape covering the front surface.
The bottom unit has a visible black label on the side, but the text is illegible.
Both units have green and blue braided cables attached.
The units appear to be made of plastic with a matte finish.
No brand names, logos, or model numbers are visible on either unit.

claims.evidence: The items look like standard power banks, but their internal condition and capacity are unknown.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.proof: A clear photo of the label on the side of the bottom unit showing the specifications.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a low-capacity generic unit

risks.proof: A video showing the unit charging a phone and the battery indicator light working.
Close-up photos of the ports and the internal battery cells.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Clear photo of the label on the bottom power bank showing the capacity (mAh) and voltage.
Video of the power bank charging a mobile device.
Photo of the ports to check for corrosion or damage.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
